questions.stem:
An agent will usually be liable under a contract made with a third party when the agent is acting on behalf of
A disclosed principal | An undisclosed principal

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
An agency relationship exists when one party (agent) acts on behalf of another (principal) in contractual dealings with a third party. The agent's liability for a contract it makes with a third party differs depending on the information the agent reveals about the principal.

When the principal's identity is fully disclosed, only the principal is liable under any contract the agent makes with a third party.

When the principal is partially disclosed, the third party knows there is a principal but does not know the principal's identity. In this case, both the agent and the principal are liable under any contract the agent makes with a third party.

When the principal is undisclosed, the third party is led to believe the agent is acting on their own behalf. In this case, the agent is liable under any contract it makes with a third party. The principal is not liable but must indemnify the agent for its liability for the contract.

A partial or undisclosed principal is often used when the principal benefits by the third party not knowing the information (wealthy principal buying multiple, plots of land).
questions.explanationJa: 代理人の契約責任は、本人についてどこまで相手方に明かしたかで決まる。本人の身元を完全に明かした場合（顕名の本人）は、本人だけが責任を負い、代理人は責任を負わない。本人の存在を明かさず、代理人が自分のために行動していると相手方に信じさせた場合（非顕名の本人）は、代理人が契約上の責任を負う。なお、本人の存在は明かしたが身元を明かさなかった場合は、本人と代理人の双方が責任を負う。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Agency Q.1

questions.stem: Which of the following acts, if committed by an agent, will cause a principal to be liable to a third party?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A negligent act committed by an independent contractor, in performance of the contract, which results in injury to a third party.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An intentional tort committed by an employee outside the scope of employment, which results in injury to a third party.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An employee's failure to notify the employer of a dangerous condition that results in injury to a third party.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A negligent act committed by an employee outside the scope of employment that results in injury to a third party.

questions.explanation:
When hiring someone for services, it is important (for liability purposes) to determine whether there is an independent contractor (IC), agency, or employment relationship.

Agency relationship: In an agency relationship, the principal has significant control over the agent. Therefore, the principal is liable for contracts and torts created by the agent acting within the scope of the relationship.

Employment relationship: An employment relationship is a special type of agency relationship that has additional legal obligations and duties (job safety rules, payroll taxes). Like an agency relationship, the employer has significant control over the employee. Based on respondeat superior, the employer is liable for contracts and torts (bodily injury) caused by the employee acting within the scope of employment.

IC relationship: In an IC relationship the IC is not subject to the control of the hiring party. Therefore, the IC (not the hiring party) is liable for all contracts and torts (bodily injury) created while performing the duties of the IC agreement ("A negligent act committed by an independent contractor, in performanc…").

("An intentional tort committed by an employee outside the scope of emp…" / "A negligent act committed by an employee outside the scope of employm…") An employer is not responsible for an employee's intentional or negligent torts when the employee is acting outside the scope of employment.
questions.explanationJa: 雇用関係は代理関係の一種であり、使用者責任（respondeat superior）により、使用者は職務の範囲内で生じた従業員の不法行為について責任を負う。危険な状態を雇用主に知らせなかったという従業員の過失によって第三者が負傷した場合、使用者である本人が責任を負う。独立契約者は委託者の支配下にないので、その過失の責任は独立契約者自身が負う。また、従業員が職務の範囲外で行った故意または過失による不法行為について、使用者は責任を負わない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Agency Q.2

questions.stem:
Part agreed to act as Young's agent to sell Young's land. Part was instructed to disclose that Part was acting as an agent but not to disclose Young's identity. Part contracted with Rice for Rice to purchase the land. After Rice discovered Young's identity, Young refused to fulfill the contract. Whom does Rice have a cause of action against?
Part | Young

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
An agency relationship exists when one party (the agent) acts on behalf of another (the principal) in contractual obligations with third parties. The principal (Young) will always be liable for the contracts the agent (Part) makes with a third party (Rice) on the principal's behalf. The agent's liability depends on the information the agent reveals about the principal to the third party.

Principal fully disclosed: If Part discloses Young's identity, then Young is the only one liable on the contract Part makes with Rice. Rice has a cause of action against Young, but not Part.

Principal partially disclosed: In this situation, Part told Rice only that Part was an agent for a principal but did not disclose Young's identity. When the principal is partially disclosed, both the agent and the principal are liable under any contract the agent makes with a third party. Therefore, Rice has a cause of action against Young and Part.

Principal undisclosed: If Part leads Rice to believe that Part is acting alone (no principal involved), then Part is liable on the contract. Young is not liable on the contract but must indemnify Part for Part's liability on it.

The agent is held liable in the partial and undisclosed situations because the third party enters the contract based on the agent's trustworthiness and reputation.
questions.explanationJa: 代理人が本人のために結んだ契約について、本人は常に責任を負う。代理人の責任は、本人について相手方に何を明かしたかで決まる。Partは代理人であることを明かしたがYoungの身元は明かしていないので、本人の部分的開示に当たり、本人と代理人の双方が責任を負う。相手方は代理人の信用を頼りに契約したと考えられるからである。よってRiceはPartとYoungの両方に請求できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Agency Q.4

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements represent(s) a principal's duty to an agent who works on a commission basis?
I. The principal is required to maintain pertinent records,account to the agent, and pay the agent according to the terms of their agreement .
II. The principal is required to reimburse the agent for all authorized expenses incurred unless the agreement calls for the agent to pay expenses out of the commission .
I | II

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
When a principal pays an agent a commission, it implies that the principal will maintain proper records of the commission calculation. In addition, if the agent requests support or evidence of the calculation, the principal is obligated to show the agent the commission records (an accounting).

A principal is obligated to reimburse an agent for all authorized expenses incurred while performing duties for the principal. However, the parties can agree that the agent must pay its own expenses out of the earned commissions instead of being reimbursed separately.
questions.explanationJa: 歩合制で報酬を支払う場合、本人は歩合の計算記録を適切に保存し、代理人から求められれば記録を示して計算を説明し（会計報告）、合意どおりに支払う義務を負う。また、本人は、代理人が職務遂行中に支出した承認済みの費用を償還する義務を負う。ただし、代理人が歩合から自分で経費を負担すると合意した場合は、別途の償還はない。よって、どちらの記述も本人の義務に当たる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Agency Q.5

questions.stem: When an agent acts for an undisclosed principal, the principal will not be liable to third parties if the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Principal ratifies a contract entered into by the agent.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Agent acts within an implied grant of authority.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Agent acts outside the grant of actual authority.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Principal seeks to conceal the agency relationship.

questions.explanation:
In an agency relationship, when an agent acts outside the authority granted by an undisclosed principal, the principal is not liable for the contract. The undisclosed principal will be liable for the contract only if it chooses to ratify the contract

("Principal ratifies a contract entered into by the agent."). Ratification occurs when the principal either:

explicitly accepts the unauthorized contract or

remains silent and accepts the benefits of the contract.

("Agent acts within an implied grant of authority.") Implied/apparent authority occurs when the principal takes an action that leads a third party to believe the agent has authority to enter contracts on the principal's behalf. Therefore, an agent can act within an implied/apparent grant of authority only if the principal is disclosed to the third party.

("Principal seeks to conceal the agency relationship.") Being undisclosed (concealed) does not alone make the principal liable for a contract the agent makes. An undisclosed principal is often used when the principal benefits from the third party not knowing the information (wealthy principal buying multiple plots of land).
questions.explanationJa: 非顕名の本人は、代理人が実際に与えた権限の範囲を越えて結んだ契約については責任を負わない。ただし、本人が契約を明示的に受け入れるか、黙って契約の利益を受け取ることで追認した場合は、責任を負う。表見代理は、本人の行動によって相手方が代理権を信じた場合に成立するものであり、本人が相手方に知られていない非顕名の場合には成立しない。本人が代理関係を隠していることだけでは、本人に責任は生じない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Agency Q.6

questions.stem: Orr gives North power of attorney. In general, the power of attorney

choices.label: A
choices.text: Will be valid only if North is a licensed attorney at law.

choices.label: B
choices.text: May continue in existence after Orr's death.

choices.label: C
choices.text: May limit North's authority to specific transactions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Must be signed by both Orr and North.

questions.explanation:
Elements of a power of attorney (POA)

Express grant of actual authority to an agent

In writing

Signed by principal

Usually notarized

Two types:

General (agent can do anything principal can do)

Limited (agent has only specific powers listed in the POA)

May or may not terminate on incapacity of principal

Always terminates on death of principal

A common form of agency is a power of attorney (POA), which is a written authorization for the agent (North) to act on behalf of the principal (Orr) for a specific or indefinite period of time. A POA may be limited, granting the agent authority to act in only certain matters, or general, granting the agent authority to act in all matters.

POAs created in anticipation of the principal's mental state deteriorating often include a specific provision keeping the POA enforceable in the event of the principal's insanity or incapacity. The POA always terminates upon the death of the principal ("May continue in existence after Orr's death."). Post-death matters (probating the will) are handled through administration of the decedent's estate.

("Will be valid only if North is a licensed attorney at law.") Anyone with legal capacity can be an agent in a POA. There are no licensing requirements (licensed attorney).

("Must be signed by both Orr and North.") A POA must be signed by the person granting it (Orr), and most states also require it to be signed and notarized by a notary public. However, the agent is not required to sign the POA.
questions.explanationJa: 委任状（power of attorney）は、本人（Orr）が代理人（North）に実際の権限を明示的に与える書面で、本人が署名し、通常は公証を受ける。委任状には、本人ができることを何でも代理できる包括的なものと、特定の事項に権限を限る限定的なものがあるので、Northの権限を特定の取引に限ることができる。代理人は弁護士である必要はなく、法的能力があれば誰でもなれ、代理人の署名も不要である。本人の無能力に備えて存続させる定めは置けるが、本人の死亡時には必ず終了する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Agency Q.7
